expectations.text: States plainly that the not-empty check is insufficient
expectations.evidence: "'Revenue table isn't empty'...and it only catches the extreme case — a completely empty table. Your actual incident produced a table that was *full of zeros*, which would pass this test."

expectations.text: Identifies the COALESCE to zero as the mechanism that made the failure silent
expectations.evidence: "The COALESCE pattern is the core hazard: it's the data equivalent of `except: pass`. It converts 'something is broken' into 'revenue is low this week'"

expectations.text: Recommends reconciliation against a source of truth, not only shape checks
expectations.evidence: "Reconciliation (Detection, but the right one): Sum revenue in your model daily against a trusted upstream total. This is the only check that catches *logic errors*"

expectations.text: Recommends that assertions run before publication rather than after, so bad data cannot reach the dashboard
expectations.evidence: Discusses detection devices and assertions but does not explicitly recommend they run before/gate dashboard publication

expectations.text: Recommends a data contract or schema check so an upstream rename fails loudly and attributably
expectations.evidence: "Data contract on the upstream table: The upstream team declares the schema; renames are breaking changes that fail your pipeline loudly instead of producing NULLs."

expectations.text: Recommends volume or null-rate assertions rather than only a non-empty check
expectations.evidence: Table shows "Is there the right amount? (volume)" and "NULL rate check on revenue column"; recommendations include "NULL rate assertion before COALESCE"

expectations.text: Treats three weeks of nobody noticing as a detection gap worth its own fix
expectations.evidence: Does not frame the 3-week silent failure as a specific detection gap requiring its own instrumentation or fix

expectations.text: Explains why a silently wrong number is more dangerous than a failed pipeline
expectations.evidence: "Three weeks of wrong numbers that 'look low' is worse than three weeks of a failing pipeline"; "In data, silence is the defect"
